The MPHC Stenographer selection process has two stages: an Online Preliminary Examination (100 marks) and a Hindi Stenography/English Stenography Skill Test (100 marks). English Stenography is held for candidates who choose the Assistant Grade-III (English Knowing) post.
The examination is common for all the posts and has multiple-choice (M.C.Q.) questions for a maximum of 100 marks
with 1 mark for each question. The duration is 120 minutes (2 hours). It may be held in one shift
or in more than one shift if required
at centres including Jabalpur
Bhopal
Indore
Gwalior
Sagar
Satna and Ujjain (all
or one or more as required). If it is held in more than one shift
the question papers will be different. The date(s)

time and centres will be published through a notice on the High Court website. The online preliminary exam date is "to be notified later". Admit cards will be available on the High Court website; the print-out facility is expected to be available about 7 days before the exam date. The candidate must enter the application number and password to download it.
Proposed model answers will be displayed on the High Court website after the preliminary examination. Objections must be submitted offline within 7 days of the notice
during office hours (10:00 AM to 05:00 PM)
to the Principal Registrar (Examination)
Administrative Building
High Court of Madhya Pradesh
Jabalpur
in the prescribed format with self-attested copies of source documents. Objections received by e-mail or any other mode are not considered. For Stenographer Grade-II
Stenographer Grade-III and Stenographer Grade-III (Court Manager Staff)
the result is prepared on the basis of marks in merit
and candidates up to a 1:5 ratio in each category (about 5 candidates per post
including all candidates with marks equal to the cut-off marks) are declared successful for the Hindi stenography skill test. For Assistant Grade-III (English Knowing)

candidates in the same 1:5 ratio are declared successful for the English stenography skill test. The preliminary examination is screening only; its marks will not be considered at the time of the final result.

Candidates who qualify must pay the ₹743.40 portal fee online to the service provider through a web link to be provided on the High Court website. Candidates who do not pay will be treated as unwilling for the skill test and their candidature will be cancelled. Candidates will be given a dictation of about 400 words in 5 minutes
followed by a separate 30 minutes for transcription. A mock dictation is given first
then the original dictation. Transcription is done on a computer; a keyboard is provided at the centre and candidates cannot bring their own computer

keyboard or chair. Hindi transcription must be done in Remington Gail. Extra time is given before the test to check the keyboard. A notebook is provided for noting down the dictation. If the dictation is written in long hand in the notebook
full marks will be deducted. In evaluation
1/2 (0.50) mark is deducted for each error (wrong words
spelling errors
omitted words
punctuation errors
extra spaces or missing spaces between words and other typing errors). If a candidate makes more than 120 errors

the answer sheet will not be evaluated further and zero (00) marks will be awarded. The date of the skill test will be published separately on the High Court website. Candidates who make noise or disturbance during dictation or transcription
or argue unnecessarily
can be removed from the examination hall and their candidature cancelled. No provision exists for re-checking marks or re-evaluation of typing
and re-examination is not allowed.
The final skill test result is prepared category-wise on merit
keeping in mind the post(s) chosen in the online form and the educational qualification. The Stenographer Grade-II result is prepared first from successful candidates
then Stenographer Grade-III
then Stenographer Grade-III (Court Manager Staff)
and then Assistant Grade-III (English Knowing)
from the remaining successful candidates. Minimum marks in the skill test for all posts: General and Other Backward Classes 55%
Scheduled Caste 45%
Scheduled Tribe and disabled candidates 40%
and EWS 49.5%. In the case of equal marks

the older candidate gets preference. The final selection list and waiting list will be published on the High Court website. The waiting list will be valid from the date of declaration of the final result as per the Madhya Pradesh General Administration Department circular No. F6-07/2012/One(1) dated 14 July 2016. Inclusion of a name in the list gives no right to appointment until the appointing authority is satisfied about the candidate's suitability after verification of documents and background. The High Court reserves the right to correct the result in the case of a computer error
clerical error or other significant error. After the final result

the Response Sheet and score card for both the preliminary examination and the skill test will be shown on the High Court website. The candidate must enter the application number as User I.D. and the password.
Bond: The selected candidate must execute a bond of ₹2
000 (two lakh rupees) in the prescribed format and commit to serve for at least three years after joining. If the candidate resigns or leaves earlier
or violates any condition of the bond
the bond becomes enforceable and the candidate must pay ₹2
000. The bond amount need not be paid if the candidate/employee resigns
with prior permission

to join service in the Government of Madhya Pradesh or the Central Government. Posting: The district is allotted through counselling on the basis of category-wise merit and category-wise availability of vacancies in districts. Candidates have no right to a particular district or post. The appointing authority for all these posts is the Principal District and Sessions Judge of the concerned district. Requests for change of district after counselling will not be considered. Travel allowance: No travel allowance of any kind is payable to candidates appearing in the online preliminary examination and skill test. Information under the Right to Information: The candidate's answer sheet/candidate response will be provided on payment of the prescribed fee for 3 months after the final selection list is issued; the response sheet data will then be destroyed. Application forms and other material used in the examination (except those of finally selected candidates) will be destroyed one year after the selection list/final result is declared.
how_to_apply: MPHC Stenographer apply online is open on the High Court of Madhya Pradesh website. Follow these steps as given in the advertisement:
Visit the High Court of Madhya Pradesh website, www.mphc.gov.in.

Click the "Recruitment/Result" button, then click "Click on-Online Application Forms/Admit Cards". Four links will be available for this recruitment: Advertisement, Registration, Application and Edit Application.
Click the Advertisement link and read the full instructions of the advertisement carefully.
Click the Registration link and enter the required information. A User-ID and Password will be sent to the mobile number and e-mail ID entered by the candidate.
Click the Application link, fill in the application form completely and upload the photo and signature.
Preview the form, click the Submit button and pay the prescribed fee through debit card or internet banking.
After successful payment, click the Print button to get a print-out of the application and keep it safe for the further steps of the examination.

Candidates must make sure that the information in the application is correct and true; a separate application for correction later will not be entertained. No provision exists for correcting entries made in the Registration form.

The Edit Application window is available from 30.10.2026 (12:00 noon) to 01.11.2026 (05:00 PM). It applies only to entries made while filling the application form. The advertisement also says that correctable errors can be corrected within 3 days after the last date of filling the online form, and that no correction can be made after this period.
For problems in filling the online form, the advertisement gives the service provider Help Desk telephone number as 919513253398 (as printed in the notification).

content_sections.heading: MPHC Stenographer Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Reservation and age relaxation apply only to original residents (domiciles) of Madhya Pradesh. Candidates from outside Madhya Pradesh must fill their category as "Unreserved" and apply only against Unreserved vacancies. OBC, SC, ST and EWS candidates of any state other than Madhya Pradesh are treated as Unreserved candidates. Disabled candidates of any state other than Madhya Pradesh apply under the UR (PH) category. EWS: 10% vertical reservation in direct recruitment vacancies. Women: 35% horizontal and compartment-wise reservation (as per the Extraordinary Gazette Notification dated 03.10.2023). Ex-servicemen: 10% horizontal and compartment-wise reservation (as per the Extraordinary Gazette Notification dated 21.04.1999). PwD: 6% reservation (as per circular dated 01.06.2022), with 1.5% each for (i) blind and low vision, (ii) deaf and hard of hearing, (iii) locomotor disability including cerebral palsy, leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims and muscular dystrophy, and (iv) autism, intellectual disability, specific learning disability, mental illness and multiple disabilities.

content_sections.heading: MPHC Stenographer Qualification
content_sections.text: As per Madhya Pradesh General Administration Department circular No. C3-07/2015/1/3 dated 18.08.2015, a one-year computer diploma course from any one of the following is mandatory: A diploma from any university recognized by the UGC. A diploma from any open university recognized by the UGC. A diploma-level examination from DOEACC/National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT). A Modern Office Management course from a Government Polytechnic College. A one-year "Computer Operator and Programming Assistant" (COPA) certificate from a Government ITI. In addition to the above computer diploma, the following qualifications are also accepted: B.E. (CSE/IT), M.C.A., B.C.A., M.Sc. (IT/CS), B.Sc. (IT/CS), M.Tech, M.E., etc. An AICTE-approved polytechnic diploma in Computer Science, Computer Application and Information Technology, etc. B.Sc./B.Com. degrees in which only one subject of computer is studied are not valid. As per General Administration Department letter No. C-3-7/2015/1/3 dated 29 May 2019, if a candidate has passed B.Sc. with IT/CS along with other subjects, and the IT/CS subject is confirmed/certified on the mark-sheet, that B.Sc. degree will also be treated as equal to a B.Sc. (I.T./C.S.) degree.

faq.question: Q1. What is the conducting body for MPHC Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The recruitment process is managed by the Madhya Pradesh High Court, Jabalpur (MPHC) for filling various stenographer and assistant positions across courts in the state of Madhya Pradesh.

faq.question: Q2. How many total vacancies are announced in this notification?
faq.answer: A total of 418 vacancies have been announced for positions including Stenographer Grade-II, Stenographer Grade-III, Stenographer Grade-III (Court Manager Staff), and Assistant Grade-III (English Knowing).

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply online for MPHC Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date to submit the online application form is 27-10-2026. Candidates must complete their registration and fee payment on or before this closing date to avoid rejection.

faq.question: Q4. What is the minimum educational qualification required?
faq.answer: Candidates must possess a Graduation degree in any discipline from a recognized university, along with a CPCT score card, relevant shorthand speed, and a one-year computer diploma.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for applying to these posts?
faq.answer: The minimum age limit is 18 years and the maximum age limit is 40 years as on 01-01-2026, with admissible age relaxations provided for reserved categories and female applicants.

faq.question: Q6. Is there any application fee for MP domicile reserved categories?
faq.answer: Candidates belonging to OBC, SC, ST, EWS of Madhya Pradesh, and all PwD applicants are exempted from paying the exam fee, though a portal fee of Rs. 743.40/- is applicable.

faq.question: Q7. What is the selection process for MPHC Stenographer and Assistant posts?
faq.answer: The selection process comprises an Online Preliminary Examination (MCQ Type) followed by a Skill Test in Hindi or English Shorthand and Typing, culminating in a Final Merit List.

faq.question: Q8. How can I apply for the MPHC Various Posts Online Form 2026?
faq.answer: Eligible candidates can apply online by visiting the official website www.mphc.gov.in, navigating to the recruitment section, filling out the registration form, and submitting details.

faq.answer: Eligible candidates can apply online by visiting the official website www.mphc.gov.in, navigating to the recruitment section, filling out the registration form, and submitting details.

faq.question: What are the salary details for Stenographer Grade-II?
faq.answer: Stenographer Grade-II positions fall under the pay scale of Rs. 5200-20200 with a Grade Pay of 2800/- corresponding to the 7th CPC Pay Matrix of 28700-91300.

faq.question: Are candidates from other states eligible to apply?
faq.answer: Yes, candidates from other states can apply under the unreserved category. However, specific reservation benefits and fee relaxations are restricted to bonafide residents of Madhya Pradesh.
